item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
ABCD is a trapezoid.

[Image: Trapezoid ABCD]

Another trapezoid, GHIJ (not shown), is congruent (the same size and shape) to ABCD. Angles G and J each measure 70°. Which of these could be true?

options.label: B
options.text: Angle H is a right angle.

options.label: C
options.text: All sides of GHIJ are the same length.

options.label: D
options.text: The perimeter of GHIJ is 3 times the perimeter of ABCD.

options.label: E
options.text: The area of GHIJ is less than the area of ABCD.

item.figure_description: An isosceles trapezoid ABCD with horizontal base AD along the bottom and shorter horizontal side BC along the top. Vertex A is at the bottom left, B is at the top left, C is at the top right, and D is at the bottom right. The interior angle at vertex A is labeled 70°, and the interior angle at vertex D is labeled 70°.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
[Image: Two triangles]

The triangles shown are congruent. The measures of some of the sides and angles are given. What is the value of x?
reference_items.figure_description:
Two triangles are shown side by side.
The left triangle has a horizontal bottom side. Its left side is labeled "6 cm". The interior angle at the bottom-left vertex is labeled "49°", and the interior angle at the top vertex is labeled "81°".
The right triangle has a nearly horizontal bottom side that slopes slightly downward from right to left, labeled "6 cm". The interior angle at the bottom-right vertex is labeled "81°", and the interior angle at the top vertex is labeled "x°".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which shape has a line of symmetry?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: A trapezoid with two parallel horizontal lines. The right side of the trapezoid is longer than the left hand side.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: An isosceles triangle with the base forming a vertical line.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: A parallelogram where top and bottom sides are equal in length and the left and right sides are also equal in length.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: A right triangle with the 90 degree angle in the bottom left.]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four geometric shapes labeled A through D:
A: A trapezoid with horizontal top and bottom parallel sides; the bottom is longer than the top, and the right slanted side is longer and less steep than the left side.
B: An isosceles triangle with a vertical base on the left and a vertex pointing to the right; the top and bottom sides are marked with equal tick marks.
C: A parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides each marked with a single tick mark, and slanted left and right sides each marked with a double tick mark.
D: A scalene right-angled triangle with a vertical left side and a horizontal bottom side, with a right-angle square symbol marked at the lower-left corner.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The line m is a line of symmetry for figure ABCDE.

The measure of angle BCD is

[Image: Polygon ABCDE with line of symmetry m]
reference_items.figure_description: A symmetric five-sided polygon ABCDE with a vertical dashed line of symmetry labeled m, which has arrows at both top and bottom ends. The horizontal top side connects vertex A on the left to vertex E on the right, bisected perpendicularly by line m. The left side goes down and outward from A to vertex B, then slants down and inward to vertex C at the bottom, which lies on line m. The right side is a mirror image, going from E down and outward to vertex D, then down and inward to vertex C. Inside the polygon, angle A is marked with an arc and labeled 130, angle B is marked with an arc and labeled 110, and the angle between side BC and line of symmetry m at vertex C is marked with an arc and labeled 30.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which of these could represent the expression 2x + 3x?

options.label: A
options.text: The length of this segment: [Image: X and 5 are segment lengths on a number line, and the segment length of 5 is slightly larger than the segment length of x.]

options.label: B
options.text: The length of this segment: [Image: 2, 3, and x are segment lengths on a number line. The segment length of 2 is the smallest. The segment length of 3 is around twice the length of 2, and the segment length of x is almost three times the length of 2.]

options.label: C
options.text: The area of this figure: [Image: A rectangle, where one side of the rectangle is labeled “x” and the other side is divided, with the smaller part labeled 2, and the larger part other labeled 3.]

options.label: D
options.text: The area of this figure: [Image: A rectangle, with one side is labeled 5 and the other side is divided in two equal parts, with each part labeled with “x”.]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four options showing visual representations:
- Option A shows a horizontal line segment with vertical tick marks at its ends, divided into two segments by an interior vertical tick mark. The segment on the left is labeled x above, and the segment on the right is labeled 5 above.
- Option B shows a horizontal line segment with vertical tick marks at its ends, divided into three segments by two interior vertical tick marks. From left to right, the segments are labeled 2, 3, and x above.
- Option C shows a rectangle with its left vertical side labeled x. A vertical dotted line extends through the rectangle, dividing the top horizontal side into two parts, labeled 2 on the left and 3 on the right.
- Option D shows a rectangle with its left vertical side labeled 5. A vertical dotted line extends through the rectangle, dividing the top horizontal side into two equal parts, each labeled x above.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Two of the triangles below are similar.

[Image: Four triangles labeled I, II, III, IV]

Which two triangles are similar?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four triangles displayed side by side:
- Triangle I: A scalene obtuse triangle with a horizontal base at the bottom. The top vertex is closer to the left, so the left side is shorter than the right side.
- Triangle II: An acute isosceles triangle with a horizontal top edge. The two longer sides point downward to meet at a sharp vertex at the bottom.
- Triangle III: A tall, thin obtuse triangle with a short horizontal base at the bottom. The left side slants steeply upward to a top vertex, which connects via a long hypotenuse-like side down to the right end of the base.
- Triangle IV: A scalene obtuse triangle with a horizontal top edge, pointing downward to a vertex at the bottom offset to the right. It has the same shape and internal angles as Triangle I, but rotated 180° and reduced in size.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
